summary: The enterprise AI model API landscape in 2026 is dominated by hyperscaler aggregators (AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI/Foundry, Google Vertex AI) that each offer dozens of foundation models behind a single secure API while keeping data inside the customer's cloud environment. There is no universal winner — the best fit usually follows an organization's existing cloud footprint, compliance needs, and preferred models. Data-platform players (Snowflake Cortex, Databricks) and governance-focused vendors (IBM watsonx) round out the market for enterprises that want AI close to their data or strong model lifecycle controls.
why_enterprises_use_aggregators: Data residency and privacy: prompts, completions, and fine-tuning data stay within the enterprise's own cloud tenant/VPC and are not used to train the provider's models, unlike calling consumer vendor APIs directly.

Compliance and certifications: aggregators inherit the hyperscaler's SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, FedRAMP, GDPR, and regional data-residency guarantees, which is far harder to satisfy with individual startup vendor APIs.
Single billing and existing cloud contracts: usage is consolidated onto the existing enterprise cloud agreement (EDP/committed spend), simplifying procurement, invoicing, and budget drawdown.

Model choice and portability: one API provides access to Claude, Llama, Mistral, Gemini, GPT, Cohere, and more, letting teams switch or route between models without rewriting integrations or signing new vendor contracts.
Enterprise security and governance: built-in IAM/RBAC, VPC/PrivateLink networking, audit logging, guardrails, and key management integrate with tooling the enterprise already operates and monitors.

platforms.name: Amazon Bedrock
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-token (on-demand) plus Provisioned Throughput reserved capacity; batch inference discounts; separate fine-tuning and custom model hosting charges.
platforms.best_for: Enterprises already on AWS wanting the widest model choice (especially Claude) under one managed, secure API.

platforms.name: Azure OpenAI Service / Azure AI Foundry
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-token plus Provisioned Throughput Units (PTUs) for reserved capacity; batch API discounts; separate fine-tuning and hosting charges.
key_features: Exclusive enterprise access to OpenAI frontier models
Content filtering and Azure AI Content Safety
Broader catalog via Azure AI Foundry
platforms.best_for: Microsoft-first shops needing GPT/OpenAI models with Entra ID, Microsoft 365, and Copilot integration under enterprise governance.

platforms.name: Google Vertex AI Model Garden
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-token for Gemini; Generative AI Scale Units (GSUs) for reserved/provisioned throughput (e.g., ~25 GSUs of Gemini 2.5 Flash ≈ 67,250 tokens/sec); separate tuning and hosting charges.
key_features: Native Gemini plus 100+ models in Model Garden
platforms.best_for: Google Cloud / data-analytics-centric enterprises wanting Gemini plus multimodal (image, video, speech) and strong MLOps tooling.

platforms.name: Snowflake Cortex AI
platforms.pricing: Consumption-based, billed in Snowflake credits by tokens/compute; no separate model contracts; integrated with existing Snowflake spend.
key_features: LLM functions run directly on governed Snowflake data
No data movement outside the Snowflake perimeter
Access history and query audit logs
platforms.best_for: Enterprises whose data already lives in Snowflake and want in-database LLM access with zero ETL and unified governance.

platforms.name: IBM watsonx.ai
available_models: Third-party open models from Hugging Face
platforms.pricing: Subscription plus consumption (Resource Units) on IBM Cloud; available on-prem and hybrid via Cloud Pak for Data / Red Hat OpenShift.
key_features: watsonx.governance for model risk and compliance
watsonx Orchestrate for enterprise AI agents
platforms.best_for: Regulated enterprises (finance, government, healthcare) needing strong AI governance, on-prem/hybrid options, and indemnified models.

platforms.name: Databricks Mosaic AI
platforms.pricing: Consumption-based (DBUs) on top of underlying cloud; pay-per-token foundation model APIs and provisioned throughput options.
key_features: Foundation Model APIs and AI Gateway
Unity Catalog governance across data and models
Model Serving within the lakehouse perimeter
platforms.best_for: Data engineering / ML-mature enterprises building custom GenAI on the lakehouse with unified data-and-model governance.

platforms.name: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) Generative AI
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-character/token on-demand and dedicated AI clusters for reserved capacity; integrated with OCI billing.
key_features: Dedicated AI clusters for isolated hosting
EU Sovereign Cloud and dedicated regions
platforms.best_for: Oracle-centric enterprises and sovereignty-sensitive workloads needing AI alongside Oracle databases and ERP applications.

platforms.name: Cloudflare Workers AI
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-use (per neuron/token) with generous free tier; serverless, no provisioned capacity required; AI Gateway billed separately.
key_features: Serverless inference at the global edge (low latency)
AI Gateway for caching, rate limiting, and analytics
Runs close to end users in 300+ cities
platforms.best_for: Developers and enterprises needing low-latency, serverless edge inference for open models and a unified gateway to multiple providers.
